title: Orchestration

purpose.mechanism: Orchestration: (a) multi-timestepping coordinates processes updating at different rates through a shared store; (b) workflow organizes processes as a dependency DAG; (c) event-driven graph rewrites (division, engulfment, bursting) modify system structure.

config.caption: Orchestration: (a) multi-timestepping coordinates processes updating at different rates through a shared store; (b) workflow organizes processes as a dependency DAG; (c) event-driven graph rewrites (division, engulfment, bursting) modify system structure.

Time series of the runnable fig02 demonstration (fig02-runnable) of Fig 2's panel (a), multi-timestepping: two processes update at DIFFERENT rates through ONE shared pool store. FastProduction (interval 1) fills pool.molecules every tick; SlowConversion (interval 5) fires every 5 ticks, converting the pool into pool.biomass. molecules ramps and saws down on the fast clock while biomass advances in coarse staircase steps on the slow clock — two rates coordinated through a shared store. Panels (b) workflow-DAG and (c) event rewrites stay schematic. From scripts/build_fig02_dynamics.py.

question: How are processes orchestrated across timescales, workflows, and structural rewrites?
